nodes.title: Continuous inhomogeneous cochain algebra
nodes.statement: For a profinite Γ and a discrete commutative Γ-ring R with continuous action, set C^q_cts(Γ,R)=C(Γ^q,R), including C^0=R. Use the inhomogeneous differential and (f∪g)(g₁,…,g_(r+s))=f(g₁,…,g_r)·(g₁⋯g_r)g(g_(r+1),…,g_(r+s)). This is a strictly associative unital cohomological DGA; d has degree +1 and d(f∪g)=df∪g+(−1)^r f∪dg on arbitrary cochains. Regard this as a DGA over Z (or the fixed coefficient subring); when the Γ-action on R is trivial it is an R-DGA. Give each cochain group and its cohomology the discrete topology for comparison in TopModuleCat Z; compactness of Γ^q and discreteness of R identify this with the compact-open topology on continuous maps. Do not inherit the pointwise function-space topology from the low-degree plain-function subgroups.
proofSteps: Form continuous maps on finite powers with pointwise additive operations. Give these groups the discrete topology, equal here to compact-open; verify every differential summand is continuous. Use the parent discrete wrappers when comparing with its low-degree plain-function quotients.
Expand the differential and cancel the adjacent face terms; the first face accounts for the translated action in the product.
Expand both bracketings of a triple cup to the same product in R. Construct the DGA through DGAInfinity, without replacing strict equality by a cohomology identity.
acceptance: For Γ=1, the unnormalized complex has C^q=R and alternating differential; H⁰=R and H^q=0 for q>0.
The (1,1) formula is a(g)·g b(h), and its class is the pinned explicitCup11.
For arbitrary f,g,h in C¹, both bracketings at (x,y,z) equal f(x)·x g(y)·xy h(z), with no cocycle hypotheses.
The degree-(1,1) rule contains −f∪dg; the unsigned formula fails over F₃ on a noncocycle of C₃.

For Γ=∏_N C₂ with trivial F₂ coefficients, use discrete H¹ in the canonical comparison. The inherited pointwise topology on continuous characters is not discrete: finitely many evaluations cannot isolate zero.

nodes.title: Canonical continuous-cohomology comparison
nodes.statement: The cohomology of continuousCochainDGA is naturally isomorphic, in every degree, to the parent roadmap continuousCohomology of the associated discrete representation. In degrees 0,1,2 the maps are the parent explicit comparison maps; the induced products agree with its graded cup and pinned explicitCup11. The comparison is an isomorphism of discrete objects in TopModuleCat Z, using the parent discrete low-degree wrappers, and in particular an additive isomorphism after forgetting topology.
proofSteps: For q≥0 send f to F(g₀,…,g_q)=g₀·f(g₀⁻¹g₁,…,g_(q−1)⁻¹g_q); the inverse evaluates F at (1,h₁,h₁h₂,…,h₁⋯h_q). Verify equivariance and the differential identities in both directions.

Use compact-open currying/uncurrying to identify jointly continuous homogeneous cochains with invariant elements of the parent TopRep.resolutionX iterated continuous-coinduction complex (with its degree shift). Profinite Γ and its finite powers are locally compact, so the inverse currying maps exist. This uses the actual parent resolution, not an additional bar-resolution interface.

Compactness and discrete coefficients make each compact-open term and its subquotients discrete. Compare in TopModuleCat Z via the parent low-degree discrete wrappers; check identity augmentation and the displayed inverse in degrees 0,1,2.

Translate the parent graded cup through these coordinates and compare its Alexander–Whitney formula with the displayed inhomogeneous cup. Check the pinned explicitCup11 representative and naturality in compatible pairs.

nodes.title: Changes of adjacent representatives
nodes.statement: For a discrete commutative Γ-ring R, existence of a continuous degree-one defining system and membership of zero in its product depend only on the H¹ input classes. Specialize the generic finite upper-triangular gauge theorem requested from DGAInfinity8 to M.0’s continuous cochain model with its fixed sign. If the Γ-action on R is trivial, d⁰=0, so each H¹ class has a unique continuous 1-cocycle representative. The Hom-system/adjacent-character conjugation formula is constructed in M.9, not assumed at this layer.
proofSteps: Refine the DGAInfinity8 request to a finite integral gauge theorem for degree-one matric defining systems, valid without rational coefficients. In a strictly upper-triangular degree-one matrix A with corner entry zero, dA+A² has only its corner entry possibly nonzero.

If a′_i=a_i+du_i, take a degree-zero upper-unitriangular matrix G=1+U with U_i,i+1=u_i and inverse the finite geometric series. Set A′=G⁻¹AG+G⁻¹dG. Its adjacent entries are a′_i and its curvature is G⁻¹(dA+A²)G, the same corner curvature. Reset its (0,n) entry to zero; this changes the corner value only by a coboundary. Thus each original H² value remains a value for the changed representatives.
Apply the inverse gauge to obtain equality of the two sets of H² values. All operations are finite sums and products, so preserve continuity. No exponential, logarithm or division is used.
For trivial Γ-action the explicit parent d⁰ is zero, so its H¹ quotient identifies cocycles without further representative choices. M.9 supplies the concrete adjacent-character conjugation formula.
acceptance: The existence of a defining system and membership of zero in the degree-one product depend only on the H¹ classes. For trivial coefficients a 1-cocycle is its unique class representative; for Hom coefficient systems, changing a_i by d⁰u_i is implemented by conjugation of the associated adjacent semidirect-product character by (−u,1). The matrix-valued comparison in M.9 must fix the chosen a_i before asserting a bijection.

nodes.title: Small-rank outer powering
nodes.statement: For 2≤n≤6 and U=UT_(n+1)(F_p), the powering action on conjugacy classes of U¹ factors through (Z/p)^×. Hence the literal outer exponent is 1 for p=2 and p for odd p. For p=3,n=6 and Q∈U¹, Q⁴=Q+(Q₀₂Q₂₄Q₄₆)E₀₆ and it is conjugate to Q by e₂₆(Q₂₄Q₄₆), using conjugation in the appropriate direction. For p=2, write Q as a product of two involutions to see Q conjugate to Q⁻¹.
proofSteps: If the derived subgroup has exponent p the factorization is immediate. For odd p the only remaining case in this range is p=3,n=6.
Compute (Q−1)³ as its unique length-three path. Conjugating Q by e₂₆(t) changes the 06 entry by −Q₀₂t; thus e₂₆(t)⁻¹Qe₂₆(t)=Q⁴ for t=Q₂₄Q₄₆.

For p=2 split the indices into blocks of sizes at most four. The block-diagonal matrix D has square one, and QD⁻¹ has square one; their product is conjugate to its inverse. Odd powering on elements of exponent at most four reduces to these two cases.
For odd p, the abelianization B has a nonzero element of order p, so no divisor not divisible by p can have the factorization. For p=2 the quotient unit group modulo 2 is already trivial.
acceptance: For Q=1+E₀₂+E₂₄+E₄₆ over F₃, Q⁴ differs from Q in 06, so omitting the cubic corner is false.

nodes.title: Bogomolov multiplier
nodes.statement: For a finite group H, let B_Bog(H) be the subgroup of ordinary H²(H,Q/Z), with trivial action, whose restrictions to every abelian subgroup vanish. Equivalently it suffices to restrict to cyclic and two-generator abelian subgroups (bicyclic subgroups). The same subgroup in canonical continuous H² uses the finite-discrete comparison.
proofSteps: Take the intersection of the kernels of the coefficient-preserving restriction maps.
For finite abelian A and divisible Q/Z, H²(A,Q/Z) is detected by alternating commutator pairings, so its restrictions to two-generator subgroups detect zero.
Use the ordinary/canonical comparison only for finite discrete groups.
acceptance: For abelian H the subgroup is zero, because H itself is one of the tests.
For H=C₂×C₂, the nontrivial alternating H²(H,Q/Z) class restricts to zero on every cyclic subgroup but is not in B_Bog(H).
The ordinary kernel maps to the continuous kernel under the finite-discrete H² isomorphism.

nodes.title: Commutativity-preserving exterior square
nodes.statement: For a group H define H⋏H by generators x⋏y and the crossed-pairing relations (xx′)⋏y=({}^x x′⋏{}^x y)(x⋏y), x⋏(yy′)=(x⋏y)({}^y x⋏{}^y y′), and x⋏y=1 whenever xy=yx, where {}^x y=xyx⁻¹. The commutator map κ:H⋏H→[H,H], x⋏y↦xyx⁻¹y⁻¹, is surjective and has central kernel.
proofSteps: Construct the presented group using the free group and normal closure of the displayed relators.
Verify the commutator identities with left conjugation, so the target map is defined and surjective.
Use the crossed relations to show diagonal conjugation by a commutator agrees with conjugation by its wedge; elements in the kernel therefore commute with every generator.
acceptance: For abelian H every generator is killed, so H⋏H=1.
κ(x⋏y)=xyx⁻¹y⁻¹ agrees with the pinned transvection convention; it is not x⁻¹y⁻¹xy.
In UT₃(F_p), κ(e₀₁(a)⋏e₁₂(b))=e₀₂(ab), which can be nontrivial.

nodes.title: Bogomolov character duality
nodes.statement: For finite H there is a natural isomorphism B_Bog(H)≃Hom(ker(κ:H⋏H→[H,H]),Q/Z). In particular κ injective implies B_Bog(H)=0. This is a natural duality statement, not a chosen self-duality of a finite abelian group.
proofSteps: Evaluate a central factor-set extension on lifted commutators; changing lifts has no effect. Commuting pairs evaluate to one precisely when the restrictions to bicyclic subgroups split.

For a free presentation F/R, the crossed presentation gives H⋏H=[F,F]/⟨[x,y]:[x,y]∈R⟩; its kernel is the quotient of R∩[F,F] by the same normal subgroup. Derive the presentation by universal crossed pairings.

A character of that kernel extends across R modulo the displayed subgroup, using the injectivity of Q/Z. Pushing out the associated central presentation extension gives the inverse H² class. The free-group lifting property verifies independence and the two inverse identities.

nodes.statement: Let G be the superdiagonal subgroup of UT_m(F_p) of degree ℓ≥1. In G⋏G every word has a collected form ∏_(k−i≥2ℓ) c_ik^(a_ik), ordered by increasing k−i and then i, with a_ik∈F_p. Hence κ is injective.
proofSteps: Expand arbitrary wedges using the crossed relations and the ordered transvection decomposition. Disjoint indices give commuting pairs and vanish.

For fixed endpoints i,k compare two permitted intermediate indices by expanding the wedge of the commuting pair e_ij e_rk and e_jk e_ir, with r=k−ℓ; the crossed relations identify the two chaining wedges. Parameter addition gives F_p-linearity and order dividing p.
The crossed commutator identity exchanges two chaining wedges with a correction of strictly greater endpoint gap. Collect by increasing gap; there are no gaps ≥m.
Apply κ and the unique ordered matrix factorization: a word in its kernel has all endpoint coefficients zero. Include the range 2ℓ≥m where G is abelian and the square is trivial.
acceptance: The degree-(m−1) subgroup is the nontrivial corner line; its exterior square is trivial because it is abelian.

nodes.title: Derived-stabilizer Bogomolov vanishing
nodes.statement: For every prime p and n≥2, B_Bog(U¹)=0 for U=UT_(n+1)(F_p).

Apply cp-endpoint-collection with gap ℓ=2 and cp-character-duality in every size. For sizes three and four U¹ is abelian (cyclic at size three). At size five it is nonabelian: [e₀₂(1),e₂₄(1)]=e₀₄(1)≠1. The general endpoint-collection proof, not an abelian-group shortcut, covers that case.
acceptance: For every prime p and n≥2, B_Bog(U¹)=0 for U=UT_(n+1)(F_p).
In UT₅(F_p), e₀₂(1) and e₂₄(1) belong to U¹ but have commutator e₀₄(1)≠1. Bogomolov vanishing must therefore use endpoint collection rather than an abelian shortcut.

nodes.title: Cyclically trivial first cohomology
nodes.statement: For a finite group G and finite G-module M, define H¹_cyc(G,M)=ker(H¹(G,M)→∏_(C≤G cyclic)H¹(C,M)). A cocycle b represents such a class exactly when b(σ)∈(σ−1)M for every σ∈G. Restriction to a subgroup and equivariant coefficient maps preserve this kernel.
proofSteps: Use the restriction maps of the parent cohomology carrier.
On ⟨σ⟩ a cocycle is a coboundary iff its value at σ lies in (σ−1)M; all other values follow by the cocycle recursion.
Apply the pointwise criterion to restrictions and coefficient maps.
acceptance: For cyclic G the kernel is zero because one factor tests G itself.
For trivial action, b(σ)∈(σ−1)M says b(σ)=0 for all σ, so the kernel is zero.
If the action factors through a cyclic quotient then the kernel is zero: it kills the action kernel and descends to that quotient.

If only χ modulo the outer exponent is specified, choose any compatible unit lift modulo d; the factorization property makes the test independent of that lift.

In basis (02,03,13,14,24), compute the contragredient matrices from the stabilizer action; there are eight cyclically trivial cocycles and four coboundaries.

nodes.title: Length-four and length-five fixed classes
nodes.statement: For n=4 or 5 and every a∈A, images of a-fixed conjugacy classes of U¹ generate B^a. For n=5 the only third-diagonal vector outside the boundary is e₁₄. For n=5 use the endpoint-zero reduction; size is five, not four. With nonzero endpoints solve the fixedness equations for b by the source’s cases a₂=0, a₃=0, a₁=0, or all nonzero.

nodes.statement: For a finite F₂[C₂]-module V and V^∨=Hom(V,F₂) with contragredient action, ordinary cup/evaluation induces a perfect pairing H¹(C₂,V^∨)×H¹(C₂,V)→H²(C₂,F₂)≃F₂. If t=σ−1, H¹(C₂,V)=ker(t)/im(t), with the analogous dual formula.
proofSteps: A 1-cocycle is determined by v with (1+σ)v=0; a coboundary is (σ−1)w. In characteristic two these are t-kernel and t-image.
Evaluation at (σ,σ) gives the cup pairing; its value agrees with evaluation on the two quotient classes.
Decompose a square-zero t into size-one and size-two Jordan blocks, or compute annihilators directly. Size-two blocks contribute zero cohomology, and the surviving size-one blocks pair perfectly.
acceptance: For a finite F₂[C₂]-module V and V^∨=Hom(V,F₂) with contragredient action, ordinary cup/evaluation induces a perfect pairing H¹(C₂,V^∨)×H¹(C₂,V)→H²(C₂,F₂)≃F₂. If t=σ−1, H¹(C₂,V)=ker(t)/im(t), with the analogous dual formula.

nodes.title: Archimedean refined lifting
nodes.statement: With the same n,p,r,s as refined-local-lifting, every continuous Γ_K→U/P that lifts to U/Z lifts to U for K=R or C. Thus Proposition 5.3 holds at every completion of a number field.

nodes.title: Local Massey vanishing
nodes.statement: For every local field K that is nonarchimedean or R or C, every prime p and n≥3, any defined n-fold product of H¹(K,F_p) classes contains zero. Choose any 1≤r,s≤n−2 with r+s=n−1, and apply refined lifting to the image in U/P of a quotient lift witnessing definedness.
proofSteps: Definedness gives Γ_K→U/Z. Its composition with U/P satisfies the hypothesis of the refined theorem.
The resulting U-lift has the original adjacent entries because P⊆U¹.
Apply the zero-membership Dwyer criterion. The restriction n≥3 is essential; no vanishing of arbitrary two-fold cup products is asserted.

nodes.title: Continuous Hom coefficient category
nodes.statement: Let R be a finite commutative ring and N₀,…,N_n finite R-modules with continuous Γ-linear actions χ_i. Use M_ij=Hom_R(N_j,N_i) with action g·f=χ_i(g)fχ_j(g)⁻¹ and composition M_ij⊗M_jk→M_ik. The complexes C^q_cts(Γ,M_ij) with composition-cup form a strict DG category on the indexed objects, and DGAInfinity supplies their matric degree-one defining systems. General coefficient systems with specified associative pairings are imported through that generic interface.
proofSteps: Use the existing internal-Hom conjugation action restricted to R-linear maps; finite N_j guarantees a continuous discrete action.
Define composition-cup by the same translated formula as the cochain algebra. Associativity of composition gives strict associativity, and the face cancellation gives Leibniz.
Instantiate the generic matric defining-system object, retaining its chosen adjacent cochains and canonical H² value in M_0n.
acceptance: With all N_i=R and trivial actions this is the ordinary continuous cochain algebra.
For rank-one F_p modules, the action on M_ij is the character χ_iχ_j⁻¹.
If N_i=0, every incoming or outgoing Hom group at that object is zero.
The cup of a_ij and a_jk at (g,h) is a_ij(g) composed with g·a_jk(h); dropping the translated action does not give the twisted equation.

Its diagonal map T→∏Aut_R(N_i) is split by block diagonal automorphisms. Let U(W) be its kernel, and U¹(W) the subgroup acting identically on each W_i/W_(i−2), with W_j=0 for j<0. When every N_i=R, the coordinate comparison identifies U(W) with the existing upper-unitriangular group and U¹(W) with its degree-two superdiagonal subgroup; T(W) is the larger group of invertible upper-triangular matrices.

For fixed diagonal character χ and chosen adjacent cocycles a_i, define α(g)=(a(g),χ(g)). This is a continuous homomorphism. Replacing a by a+d⁰u conjugates α by (−u,1); the H¹ input classes alone therefore specify a conjugacy class of such α, not a distinguished homomorphism.

Form the finite extension 1→Z(W)→T(W)→T(W)/Z(W)→1 and its H² class u with the induced conjugation coefficient action. Pulling along any lift of twistedAdjacentCharacter gives exactly the prescribed M_0n Galois action.

Defining systems with these adjacent entries correspond bijectively to continuous lifts α_Λ:Γ→T(W)/Z(W) of this α. In block entries, a_ij(g)=(α_Λ)_ij(g)χ_j(g)⁻¹ and conversely (α_Λ)_ij(g)=a_ij(g)χ_j(g). The attached value is −α_Λ* u in H²(Γ,M_0n).
